findings.issue: Redundant wording: the parenthetical '(do ônibus)' duplicates 'o ônibus' that appears right after; natural-pt field should not carry gloss-style parentheticals.
findings.current: Não desça (do ônibus) até o ônibus parar.
findings.suggested: Não desça até o ônibus parar.

findings.issue: Person mismatch: jp is subjectless (default first person, typical clinic phrase) and pt says 'Tenho alergia' (I), but en says 'He'. en and pt contradict each other; first person is the natural reading.
findings.current: He is allergic to house dust.

findings.issue: Duplicate tokenization: tokens 0-1 (ハウス, ダスト, all fields null) AND token 2 (compound ハウスダスト) are all present, so concatenated surfaces read ハウスダストハウスダストに… and no longer reconstruct jp.
findings.current: ハウス / ダスト / ハウスダスト (parts and compound all listed)
findings.suggested: Delete the two null part-tokens ハウス and ダスト; keep only the compound token ハウスダスト.

findings.issue: Object particle を left as を, breaking the corpus phonetic convention (を→お) that is applied elsewhere (e.g. は→わ in this batch); romaji already has 'o'.
findings.current: ぱーてぃーをひらいたらどうですか。
findings.suggested: ぱーてぃーおひらいたらどうですか。

findings.issue: lit_en is just a copy of the natural en and does not mirror the JP conditional structure, unlike lit_pt ('Se (você) abrisse/desse uma festa, como seria?'); the two literal fields should match.
findings.suggested: If (you) threw a party, how would it be?

findings.issue: Garbled/false classification in the pt-BR note: '(一段→godan)' — 開く is a plain godan verb; there is no ichidan→godan conversion. Confusing wrong grammar info for learners; the en note correctly omits it.
findings.current: raiz de 開く (一段→godan) na forma que se liga a たら: 開いたら (condicional)
findings.suggested: raiz de 開く na forma que se liga a たら: 開いたら (condicional)

findings.issue: Dictionary-form + ところです means the action is about to start, not underway; 'is just beginning' implies it has already started. pt ('prestes a começar'), lit_en and both expl fields all correctly say 'about to begin' — en is the inconsistent outlier.
findings.suggested: The party is just about to begin.

findings.issue: Dated, opaque idiom: 'green around the gills' means looking sick/queasy, while jp/pt say the person seems low on energy (元気がないみたい, 'meio sem energia'); 'My,' also misrenders attention-getting ねえ. Beginner-facing en should be plain and match the pattern.
findings.current: My, you're looking green around the gills.
findings.suggested: Hey, you seem a bit down.

findings.issue: The natural-pt field is not natural Brazilian Portuguese: gloss-style parenthetical '(aconchego)' plus the dangling apposition 'coisa nenhuma,' produce an ungrammatical comma-spliced string; literal mirroring belongs in lit_pt only.
findings.current: Calor humano (aconchego), coisa nenhuma, não se encontra em lugar algum.
findings.suggested: Calor humano é coisa que não se encontra em lugar nenhum.
